subject: Novaloq benchmarking & acceptance evidence exchange
messages:
From: Meera Singh <meera.singh@novaloq.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Benchmarking kickoff + acceptance criteria request

Hi Irene / Monica,

Thanks again for the onboarding walkthrough yesterday. We want to lock down a brief benchmarking/acceptance run before we flip traffic. High level acceptance goals from our side:
- Sustained throughput: 150–180 RPS (concurrent user mix attached)
- p95 latency <= 250 ms for short responses (~64 tokens)
- tail latency (99th) < 2.0s under production traffic profile
- Error rate < 0.5% over 30m sustained window

Can you confirm Redwood's test plan and what evidence artifacts you can provide (raw telemetry, aggregated SLO graphs, request/response samples with obfuscated PII)? We're flexible with test windows but prefer next week (UTC-7 mornings).

Also: we'll need a short statement that the run used the same model/config you intend to serve (quantization / KV cache policy). I've attached our simplified traffic mix and a small sample payload set.

-Meera
--
Meera Singh
Head of Platform Engineering, Novaloq Health
meera.singh@novaloq.com
From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Meera Singh <meera.singh@novaloq.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-24T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking kickoff + acceptance criteria request

Meera — thanks for the clear targets. Proposed approach from Redwood:

1) Two-phase benchmark run (same order as we discussed):
   - Phase A: Ramp & stabilization (45m). Gradually ramp to target RPS to warm KV caches and observe steady-state p95.
   - Phase B: Sustained window (30m) at target RPS with the production traffic mix you provided.

2) Test environment / config:
   - Model: model-redwood-3b-v2 (fp16, int8 quant profile disabled for this run)
   - Serving mode: Dedicated pool in us-west with autoscale disabled for stability (we'll allocate a fixed pod set matching expected capacity).
   - Prefix/KV cache: pre-warm using the sample prefixes you attached; cache hit-rate reported separately.

3) Evidence we will deliver immediately after the run:
   - Raw request/response log sample (PII obfuscated) — novaloq-telemetry-sample.json
   - Aggregated SLO graphs (qps, p50/p95/p99, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization) in an exportable CSV and PNG
   - A short written acceptance statement confirming the model/config used and that the run matched the stated traffic mix

4) Practical notes and asks from Novaloq:
   - Provide a short list of any queries we should exclude as known noisy tests (e.g., long generation jobs).
   - Confirm whether redirects/attachments are part of user flows (affects payload sizes).

Proposed window: 2028-07-26 09:00–11:00 PT for Phase A + Phase B combined. If that works, we'll drop the scripts and JMeter-style load file (novaloq-loadscript-v1.jmx) into the Drive link and create a temporary test token scoped to the test endpoints.

I'll loop Aditya in for deal logistics / formal acceptance artefacts.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Meera Singh <meera.singh@novaloq.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-24T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking kickoff + acceptance criteria request

Thanks — quick CS playbook items from my side so teams have a mutual action plan:

- Pre-test (T-48h): upload final loadscript & sample payloads to shared Drive, confirm obfuscation rules, and exchange test token.
- Test day: Redwood runs the two-phase script. Novaloq observes via live Grafana link (read-only).
- Post-test (T+2h): Redwood shares a results packet (artifact list above) and a one-page verdict with pass/fail vs. acceptance gates.

Acceptance gates (pass if all true):
  * sustained p95 <= 250ms
  * sustained RPS within 10% of requested target
  * p99 < 2.0s
  * error rate under 0.5%

If one gate fails we'll run a targeted remediation round (30–60m) to tune batching/route config and re-run the sustained window.

I'll be the primary CS contact during run — contact me on Slack if something shows up during execution.

—Monica
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

Adding a quick commercial note: once you confirm the acceptance run passes we'll move to the final acceptance sign-off for DEAL-2109 and enable the agreed Dedicated pool billing terms. If you need a short formal statement for procurement that the run was executed against the same model/config that will be used in production, let us know — we can generate that in the results packet.

Also flagging that any extended remediation runs may affect capacity reservations for the week; we can reserve a small buffer but please try to keep remediation to the same day.

Thanks — Aditya
